121	as it is written, "by the hand of the prophets I use similitudes." So these images
122	and these revelations are called tzimtzumim, and they are called "garments."
123	But without these garments it is impossible to grasp HaShem at all, without
124	the garments it is impossible, only through garments. And therefore
125	all of Kabbalah is based on this: that all the worlds, sefirot, and partzufim
126	are really garments and clothing for the supernal lights, so that
127	the lower beings will be able to receive these lights, to receive them at all.
128	Okay?
129	So here the Rebbe writes: divine perceptions can only be attained through
130	many contractions, from cause to effect, from a higher intellect to a lower intellect,
131	as will be explained further on in this Torah, that the higher intellect means Chochmah,
132	and the lower intellect is Malchut.
133	In the secret of the sefirot, yes, it is written, "How many are Your works, HaShem,
134	You made them all with wisdom."
135	Our Rabbis, the Kabbalists, write that...
136	the word "asita" comes from "asiyah," and asiyah is like the world of Asiyah, which corresponds to the sefirah of Malchut.
137	And the light of Chochmah is clothed in Malchut, and through this
138	it is revealed in the lower worlds.
139	And so Rabbi Nachman also writes in the first Torah of Likutei Moharan, called Torat Ayelet Chen.
140	And so it is written, "How many are Your works, HaShem, You made them all with wisdom."
141	The moment you say the words "wisdom" and "You made," that is the clothing of Chochmah in Malchut.
142	Understood?
143	And here in this Torah we will see that the higher intellect, the Rebbe calls
144	the higher intellect Chochmah, and the lower intellect is Malchut.
145	The Rebbe writes here: as we see with our senses, that one cannot grasp a great
146	intellect except through its clothing in the lower intellect.
147	The meaning of the words:
148	I want to give a parable, gentlemen, and illustrate this so it will be understood.
149	The Rebbe says here, "as we see with our senses."
150	When the Rebbe says "as we see with our senses," and these are also the words of the Arizal,
151	"as we see with our senses," or "as we see with the eyes," and so on, they mean,
152	gentlemen, that you should look at our world,
153	at concepts you know, and you will understand what I want to tell you.
154	So I will give you an example.
155	Suppose there is a great rabbi, a great teacher, who is now teaching his student
156	a certain matter, and he sees that the student has difficulty understanding the concepts.
157	So if he is a good teacher, he knows how to teach, in what manner to teach,
158	he needs to enter the student's mind, into the concepts the student does know,
159	into examples.
